verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2, because the panel raised none. The problem is stated with a reproducer in message #1, and a second case without a pooler is reported in message #14. v5 stays inside pgbench.c and its TAP test and uses the existing PQsendPrepare(), which is what message #9 asked for. Confidence is medium because nobody has reviewed v5 in the visible thread and the code was not read.

brief.title: Pgbench: make prepare asynchronous with -M prepared
brief.problem: With -M prepared, pgbench prepares each command with the blocking PQprepare(), so one waiting prepare stalls every client on the same worker thread. The author hit this behind PgBouncer in session pooling mode with more clients than the pool size. A reviewer added that a prepare waiting on a table lock stalls unrelated clients the same way.
brief.proposed_design: v5 replaces PQprepare() in sendCommand() with the asynchronous PQsendPrepare() and adds a new state, CSTATE_WAIT_PREPARE_RESULT, which waits for the result through the event loop. A new helper reads the sqlstate from an error result without reading from the connection. The pipeline path stays synchronous on purpose, and the earlier design with a new libpq function was dropped.
user_visible_surface: pgbench -M prepared no longer blocks the worker thread while a Prepare waits.
Error output on a failed prepare changes: the extra "prepared statement ... does not exist" error no longer follows a syntax error.
No libpq API change in v5; v1 to v3 added PQsendPBES to libpq exports.
author_claims: The fix makes -M prepared usable behind PgBouncer in session pooling mode when clients exceed the pool size.
Prepare time stays in --report-per-command because v5 sends the query from the new state without resetting the command timer.
A reviewer said the patch resolves the blocking with no regressions in their testing.
A new TAP test shows one client progressing while another waits on a locked table during Prepare.
brief.thread_state: Robert Haas rejected the new libpq entrypoint and asked for PQsendPrepare(); the author moved to a pgbench state machine change, which Andrey Borodin supports. v5 answers Borodin's review points, and no one has reviewed v5 in the visible thread.
unclear: Whether the split wait state fully removes blocking PQgetResult() calls, including on connection failure between results.
Whether Robert Haas accepts the v4/v5 approach.
When the pipeline path, prepareCommandsInPipeline(), will get the same fix, and whether anyone tracks it.
Whether the docs change from message #2 is still in v5, which touches only pgbench.c and the test file.

Do retry and failure counts under --max-tries and --failures-detailed stay the same when a Prepare fails in the new state?
Is there a plan or a tracking item to give prepareCommandsInPipeline() the same asynchronous treatment?

committability.owner_note: Robert Haas took part in the thread and asked for PQsendPrepare(), but he has not commented on v5. The owner needs to know the pgbench client state machine and libpq asynchronous result handling.
committability.liability: The owner signs for one more state in the pgbench state machine and for the changed error output on a failed prepare. The risk is limited to pgbench runs with -M prepared.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted five versions over about eight months, dropped the libpq function after the objection in message #9, and answered the review points in v5.

priority.reason: The fix helps pgbench users who run -M prepared with fewer threads than clients, behind a pooler or under lock waits. v5 is a 14.7 KB patch to pgbench.c and one TAP test with no libpq change, and it waits for a review of v5.

provisional_note: Without the code, the panel could not check that the new state has no blocking PQgetResult() left, handles connection loss, and keeps failure counting and --report-per-command timing unchanged.

precedents_retrieved.title: New GUC prepared_statement_limit to limit memory used by prepared statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, prepared_statement_limit, that caps the memory each session uses for saved CachedPlanSources, keeping them in an LRU list and invalidating query lists and generic plans when the limit is exceeded. It also changes the plan cache invalidation callbacks to free invalidated query lists at once instead of only marking them invalid.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was returned with feedback because the author did not update it in the months after review. Reviewers had found it crashed in the regression tests: Tom Lane traced this to freeing data inside PlanCacheRelCallback and similar callbacks while outer call levels may still be using it. Tom Lane also doubted the design. A cache size limit risks sudden performance drops, only the regeneratable parts of an entry are freed, the limit applies to total rather than freeable usage, and CachedExpressions are not covered. Kyotaro Horiguchi noted that measuring memory through context stats is too expensive and that there was no consensus on how to prune caches in general.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It's hard to tell where performance is going to fall off a cliff if you limit the cache size.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve handling of OOM errors in libpq making process hangling for COPY and bind (take 2)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes libpq hangs on out-of-memory errors while it parses COPY start and ParameterDescription messages. The parser leaves pqParseInput3 on error and keeps the first error message, so PQgetResult and PQexecFinish return the failure and do not wait for server input that will not come.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas committed the ParameterDescription fix but did not commit the COPY part. He could not see why the PQexecFinish change was needed, and he found that if getCopyResult() fails with OOM, libpq stays in COPY_IN mode while PQexec() returns NULL, so the next PQexec() fails with "another command is already in progress". Michael Paquier later reported that Heikki could not convince himself the change was sane for the COPY protocol, and planned more testing with tools that use COPY through libpq.
matched_queries: libpq new send function parse bind execute
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, libpq is already in PGASYNC_COPY_IN mode, but PQexec() returned NULL because of the OOM, so the application doesn't know that it's in copy mode.

precedents_retrieved.title: cursors with prepared statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `DECLARE cursor_name CURSOR FOR prepared_statement_name [ USING param, ... ]` so a cursor can be declared over a prepared statement. It attaches USING to DECLARE because direct SQL has no OPEN command, and it changes the ECPG parser to override the new main-parser rules.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas objected to the USING clause on DECLARE as a non-standard extension and proposed `DECLARE c CURSOR FOR EXECUTE p (foo, bar)` instead. Robert Haas supported the author's syntax, and the discussion stopped in July 2018 with no agreement. After months without activity and no reply to a status inquiry, Dmitry Dolgov marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I hope it's not another abandoned patch, but due to lack of response I'm
marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: query logging of prepared statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops repeating the prepared statement text in the log on every bind and execute, for both SQL EXECUTE and protocol-level PQexecPrepared, to cut log volume. Later versions log the text at Parse instead and, following a suggestion from Alvaro Herrera, use a flag in the portal so the statement is logged once.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera found that v2 dropped the statement text for unnamed statements under log_statement=all, so the patch needed more work. Andres Freund then objected to logging the statement only once: with long-running connections and many executions of one prepared statement, the query text would be far back in the log file or in an earlier rotated file. The author said he would tentatively withdraw the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm sympathetic to the desire to reduce log volume, but I'm fearful this would make log analysis much harder.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adding column "mem_usage" to view pg_prepared_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a column mem_usage to the view pg_prepared_statements that reports the memory used by each prepared statement's CachedPlanSource contexts, including the generic plan. It did not recurse into child memory contexts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund argued against separate memory reporting for each object type and proposed a general function that walks memory contexts from TopMemoryContext and reports owning objects such as prepared statements, cursors and caches. He also objected that a new column would make pg_prepared_statements more expensive for clients that query it automatically. The author agreed to rewrite the patch around a general memory view, but no new version was posted, and Alvaro Herrera noted the patch no longer applied and the discussion had not produced a code revision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm just not sure that adding separate
infrastructure for various objects is a sutainable approach.

precedents_retrieved.title: Simplify standby state machine a bit in WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the standby state machine in WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable() set currentSource to XLOG_FROM_PG_WAL after a failed archive read, so XLogFileReadAnyTLI() no longer falls back to pg_wal itself. The current source is then passed to XLogFileReadAnyTLI() directly, without the XLOG_FROM_ANY special case.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier showed that the patch undoes commit 4d894b41. On HEAD, XLogFileReadAnyTLI() checks the archive and then pg_wal for each timeline in turn. With the patch it checks the archive for all timelines and only then pg_wal, so a segment with a higher TLI in pg_wal is no longer preferred. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And this patch basically undoes that, meaning that we would basically look at the archives first for all the expected TLIs, but only if no files were found in pg_wal/.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench stopped supporting large number of client connections on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the socket checks in pgbench and in the parallel code of reindexdb and vacuumdb so that Windows can use more than about 90 client connections or jobs. On Windows, socket values can be at or above FD_SETSIZE even when few sockets are in use, so the patch checks the fd_set count instead of the socket value.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding, and the entry stayed "Waiting on Author" across several commitfests until it was closed. Fabien COELHO objected that the patch relies on the internals of the Windows fd_set structure, which an earlier version had been rejected for. David Steele suggested the problem is a limitation that could be documented instead of fixed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now your patch is basically resurrecting that. Why not if there is no other solution, but this is quite depressing, and because it breaks the interface it would be broken if windows changed its internals for some reason:-(

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to change GUCs to be able to change protocol extension parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a protocol message that lets a client set a GUC without a SET command, so poolers can see the change and some parameters can be set only at the protocol level. Over time the work became a patch set with a protocol minor version bump, min_protocol_version and max_protocol_version libpq options, and protocol parameters such as report_parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry and moved the remaining protocol patches to the thread about longer cancel keys. Some pieces were committed here, including a libpq function PQfullProtocolVersion added in place of redefining PQprotocolVersion. The visible messages show no objection that rejected the core design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This required another rebase, but I've decided that I think it'll be most fruitful to continue the discussion on protocol changes in the thread about longer cancel keys[1].

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier attempt at this idea. The thread mentions no earlier discussion of it. Within the thread, v4/v5 drops the libpq entrypoint that message #9 objected to and uses PQsendPrepare(), which is what messages #9 and #11 asked for, so no earlier rejection reason still applies.

v5 changes only pgbench.c and its TAP test, with no new option, GUC, syntax or libpq export, so the user-facing contract stays as it is. The one visible change, dropping a follow-on "prepared statement does not exist" error after a syntax error, explains the real failure better; message #8 accounts for it and the test was updated. Without the code I could not check whether retry or failure counting under --max-tries and --failures-detailed changes for prepare errors.

v5 touches only pgbench.c and its TAP test. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or libpq ABI change, because the earlier PQsendPBES export was dropped. It uses existing protocol messages through PQsendPrepare(), so this angle finds nothing to object to.

The proposal changes how pgbench, a client benchmark tool, waits for a Prepare result. It adds no privilege, role, GUC, catalog entry or server-side code, and v5 no longer changes the libpq API. The only privilege-related point is that pgbench runs with whatever rights its connection role has, and that does not change, so this angle has no objection.

From the maintenance angle v5 is local to pgbench.c and its TAP test, adds no libpq export, and costs nothing for runs without -M prepared. Two committers have engaged (messages #9, #11, #14), and the synchronous pipeline path was accepted in the thread as a scope choice. Without the code I could not check that the new state has no blocking PQgetResult() left and handles connection loss.

No existing feature gives the same result: -M extended uses unnamed statements, and --jobs equal to --client only hides the stall by spending one thread per client. v5 uses the existing PQsendPrepare() and the existing pgbench event loop, so it adds no second mechanism.

The thread shows enough demand for a fix this local. A reproducible stall behind PgBouncer in session pooling mode is reported in message #1. Message #14 adds a second case without a pooler: a Prepare waiting on a table lock stalls unrelated clients on the same worker, which skews what pgbench measures. Running with --jobs equal to --client, or using -M extended, avoids the stall, but neither keeps -M prepared measurements valid with fewer threads than clients. The cost stays inside pgbench, with no libpq or UI change in v5.
